blocks.text: Imagine a software system where a single function call can perform different operations depending on the object type. This is the power of inheritance and polymorphism in object-oriented programming.

blocks.markdown: Inheritance and polymorphism are core concepts of object-oriented programming that allow for flexible and reusable code. Inheritance enables a new class, called a subclass, to inherit properties and behaviors from an existing class, known as a superclass. Polymorphism allows objects to be treated as instances of their parent class, enabling a single interface to control different underlying forms.

blocks.title: Inheritance
blocks.text: Inheritance is a mechanism where a new class derives properties and behaviors (methods) from an existing class.

blocks.title: Polymorphism
blocks.text: Polymorphism allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common superclass. The specific method that is invoked is determined at runtime.

blocks.markdown: To understand these concepts, let's consider a simple example involving animals. We can have a superclass `Animal` with a method `makeSound()`. Subclasses like `Dog` and `Cat` can override this method to provide their specific sounds.

blocks.title: Defining a Subclass
blocks.prompt: Define a subclass `Dog` that inherits from a superclass `Animal` and overrides the `makeSound()` method.

steps.text: 1. Define the superclass `Animal` with a method `makeSound()`.
2. Define the subclass `Dog` using the `extends` keyword to inherit from `Animal`.
3. Override the `makeSound()` method in `Dog` to print `Bark`.

blocks.markdown: The above example illustrates how `Dog` inherits from `Animal` and overrides the `makeSound()` method. This is a basic form of polymorphism where the method to be executed is determined by the object's class at runtime.

blocks.title: Dynamic Dispatch
blocks.text: Dynamic dispatch is the process of selecting which implementation of a polymorphic operation (method) to call at runtime.

blocks.markdown: The substitution principle, also known as the Liskov Substitution Principle, states that objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of a subclass without affecting the functionality of the program.

blocks.title: Violation of Substitution Principle
blocks.text: If a subclass overrides a method in a way that changes the expected behavior, it can violate the substitution principle, leading to unexpected results.
